content:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: Pager: Multiple API edge TLS handshake failures from multiple regions. Observed spike in 5xx/522/525s from EU/ME/NA edge POPs. Alert rule: api.edge_5xx_rate > 5% for 5m. Root TS: 1772000000

jess (oncall): acknowledging, starting triage. Are we seeing DNS or TLS?

kiran (sre): seeing lots of TLS alert logs — openssl shows handshake failures from certain CF POPs. Running quick checks now.

sam (eng-runtime): adding logs: Prod-inbound LB showing connection resets from 172.x.x.x (Cloudflare ranges). No origin errors.

jess (oncall): eva, start customer impact comms: which customers are affected? high-level first then we can drill into tenants.

eva (support): already pulling top-10 by error rate. Early look: public hosted API endpoints mainly in EU and ME. Dedicated customers with direct peering (private) seem less impacted. Creating a ticket template for status page.

kiran (sre): quick curl check from a eu test box:
```
$ curl -v https://api.redwood-inference.com/health --resolve api.redwood-inference.com:443:104.18.20.1
* About to connect() to api.redwood-inference.com port 443 (#0)
* Trying 104.18.20.1... connected.
* TLS handshake fails: SSL_connect returned=1 errno=0 state=SSLv3 read server certificate B: certificate verify failed
* Closing connection 0
```
Points at CF edge terminating TLS or misconfigured handshake.

cloudflare-bot: Cloudflare status page: https://www.cloudflarestatus.com/incidents/xyz — reporting TLS handshake errors in multiple PoPs; root cause under investigation.

jess (oncall): good, CF is reporting a partial outage. Can we route traffic away from affected PoPs? Sam, can we force fallback to alternate edge via origin header or change TTLs?

sam (eng-runtime): We can modify our Cloudflare load-balancing / geo steering rules if we have access. For hosted customers we rely on CF route decision. Options: 1) request CF to reroute/disable problematic POPs, 2) temporarily increase HTTP keepalive so fewer handshakes, 3) move critical customers to a reserved ingress hostname (not ideal).

mike (sre): I’ve opened an enterprise ticket with CF and escalated to account rep — ticket #CF-77788. Asking for immediate POP isolation.

jess (oncall): eva please draft external comms: status page update + one-line email to top 20 customers. Include mitigation steps and ETA TBD.

eva (support): drafting now. Will post to status with severity: Partial service disruption, impact: API requests failing for some regions. ETA: monitoring.

kiran (sre): running packet capture, seeing TLS ClientHello reaching CF, but CF not completing handshake to origin — looks like CF edge is failing before origin. No CA chain issues on our end; origin certs valid.

sam (eng-runtime): confirm origin certs: issuer: Let'sEncrypt R3, expiry: 2026-08-12. Not the cause.

jess (oncall): temporary mitigation: put a bypass route that points a subdomain to direct IPs (not via CF) for internal health checks and for a subset of customers that accept it. Risky but reduces customer impact. Thoughts?

mike (sre): we should avoid exposing origin IPs publicly. If we do this, use auth-token header and only share with limited customers. Alternatively, CF allows "Always Online" fallback? But not applicable for TLS handshake failures.

sam (eng-runtime): we can spin up a temporary TLS-terminating proxy in our VPC (nginx with valid cert) and advertise it to a small set of pilot customers over private route/peering. Preparing a runbook now.

jess (oncall): ok small blast radius. Kiran, keep working on logs & packet captures. Mike, keep CF ticket hot and ask for POP drain/isolate. Sam, prep proxy and I'll coordinate pilot list with Eva.

kiran (sre): CF account rep responded: they can disable affected POPs and recommend failover to healthier PoPs; ETA 10m for initial action.

incident-bot: incident updated: severity -> Sev2. Incident owner -> jess (oncall). Pager silenced for follow-ups.

mike (sre): CF has started draining POPs listed in the ticket. Early telemetry shows error rate dropping in NA but EU still noisy.

eva (support): Published status update: https://status.redwood.com/incident/2026-03-15-cf-tls — initial comms sent to customers with opt-in for a direct fallback proxy. A few enterprise customers requested immediate peering changes.

jess (oncall): handoff — i need to go offline for 1hr, mike you take primary on-call. I'll leave runbook and current mitigation steps in the thread.

mike (sre): taking over. Summary for handoff: CF POP TLS handshake failures impacting EU/ME; CF draining affected POPs; partial recovery in NA; mitigation: pilot direct proxy for 3 enterprise customers, support comms live. Will escalate if error rate > 3% for next 10m.

kiran (sre): additional note: observed increased TLS 525 responses correlated with specific Cloudflare ASN ranges — forwarding to CF for targeted isolation.

mike (sre): implemented nginx proxy in VPC with TLS termination + auth header, spun up endpoints for pilot. Pilot customers: acme-corp, blobai, datastore-io (consent obtained). Connectivity tests look good from our test agents.

ev a (support): (typo) eva: three enterprise customers switched to proxy, all reporting decreased errors. Rolling outreach to others.

cloudflare-bot: update: partial mitigation: isolated 4 PoPs; monitoring.

mike (sre): telemetry after 30m: global 5xxs down from 8.3% -> 2.1%. EU remains at 3.9% (improving). Leaving this as Sev2 until <1% sustained.

jess (oncall): back online, thanks team. I'll run post-incident checklist in 30m and capture a timeline. Mike, keep CF ticket open until full recovery and request RCA.

sam (eng-runtime): reminder: collect packet captures and CF edge logs for postmortem correlation. Also add a fallback capability to runbook for automated proxy enabling (future work).

mike (sre): will keep monitoring, will update status when we hit <1% for 30m. Next steps: post-incident report, timeline, customer impact summary, list of customers routed to proxy, and action items for permanent routing/DR.

incident-bot: incident resolved? No — still monitoring.

(30m later)

mike (sre): update final: error rate sustained at 0.6% globally for 35m. CF confirmed full POP health restored. Closing mitigations: decommissioning temporary proxies. Requesting CF RCA and timeline from account rep.

eva (support): status update posted: incident moved to mitigated, customers notified of resolution, support follow-ups queued.

jess (oncall): closing handoff notes: root cause likely Cloudflare edge TLS regression in specific PoPs. Action items: 1) automate emergency proxy spin-up (P0 runbook), 2) add CF POP health to alarms, 3) run dedicated-latency tests across CF ASNs. I'll draft postmortem. :white_check_mark:

mike (sre): leaving final logs and ticket references in thread. Good job team. :thumbsup:
